summary: Robert P. Weller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins University (1975–1981). He became a professor at Boston University in 1990 and taught Linda Learman.

Robert Paget Dewhurst (1869–1935) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford in 1888, served there as University Lecturer in Hindustani in 1924, and taught Harold Walter Bailey.

Robert Ripley Moore (1933–1966) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bethel College (B.A. ~1952–1956) and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. ~1960–1965), later teaching at Mussoorie College and serving as Assistant Professor of Indo-Aryan Linguistics at UW-Madison (~1965–1966).

Robert S. Ellwood (1933–2025) was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago (~1964–1967) under Mircea Eliade, later serving at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson (1947–) is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Rice University and New York University. He served as professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005–2021).

Robert S. P. Beekes (1937–2017) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under doctoral supervisor F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).

Robert Schram (1850–1923) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned his Ph.D. and PD at the University of Vienna (1869–1874). He worked at the Geneva Observatory, the Militärgeographisches Institut, and the University of Vienna (~1887–1923).

Robert Sewell (1845–1925) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who attended Radley College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894), as Keeper of the Tamil Nadu Archives, and as a Fellow at the University of Madras.
Robert Seymour Conway (1864–1933) was a linguist who was educated at the City of London School. He held posts at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Tegethoff is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Cologne (2015–2018) and held posts at the Free University of Berlin, including a postdoc in 2026.
Robert Vane Russell (1873–1915) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1892–1895) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1893 to 1915.
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and under adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao (both attested 1994).

Robert Watson Frazer (1854–1921) was an Indologist educated at Rathmines School and Trinity College Dublin under Robert Atkinson. A former Indian Civil Service member, he lectured in Telugu and Tamil at UCL (1885–1916) and SOAS (1917–1919).

Robert Wilson Ievers (1850–1905) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who earned an M.A. at Queen's University Belfast. He served as a civil servant in the Ceylon Civil Service starting in 1872.

Robert Xavier Murphy (1803–1857) worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology. He served as a master at the Bombay Native Education Society and as secretary of the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry in 1839.

Robert Zimmermann (1874–1931) studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin (Ph.D. 1908–1913) under Heinrich Lüders. A scholar of Indology and Buddhism, he was Professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and Director of Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos (1957–) is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1974–1981). He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1999–2000) and the University of Munich (~2000–2023).

Robert van Gulik (1910–1967) worked in Sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University and Utrecht University (Ph.D. 1930–1935) under Jan Gonda, C. C. Uhlenbeck, and J. J. L. Duyvendak, later becoming Professor at Utrecht in 1967.

Robert von Heine-Geldern (1885–1968) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at Munich and Vienna (Ph.D. ~1910–1914) under Wilhelm Schmidt. He held posts at the University of Vienna, Columbia University, and the Asia Institute.

Robert von Schlagintweit (1833–1885) was an academic in geography, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Munich (~1851–1854). In 1864, he became Professor of Geography at the University of Giessen.
